name: context-script-v1
what: One line, the same words for every test, that means something different depending on who says it and why. The genome's job is to bring out one character's reading from these fixed words. Its plain render in every validation voice is the baseline for every later test (backend/evaluation/baseline.py --script).
rules: The words never change: only the delivery (stress, pauses, pace, pitch, breath, laughter) may change the meaning.
The line names no emotion and no relationship, so every character below can say it naturally.
Plain words, no digits or abbreviations, because the renderer runs without a text normaliser.
Two sentences, 14 words (about 5 s), long enough for a stable similarity measure (LIMITATIONS.md).

lines.text: So you finally came back. I kept everything exactly the way you left it.
lines.kind: love, grief, menace, bitterness, relief or comedy, depending on the character

readings.character: A parent whose grown child comes home after years away
readings.reading: warm, tearful joy; breath before the second sentence; soft on "exactly"

readings.character: A widow speaking at a grave
readings.reading: grief; slow, breaking voice; long pause after "back"

readings.character: A villain who has been waiting for the hero
readings.reading: cold menace; low and slow; stress on "finally"; a smile in the voice
unsettling calm; too gentle, too even; lingering on "exactly"

readings.character: A partner who was left without a word
readings.reading: bitter and hurt; clipped first sentence; flat, controlled second

readings.character: A loyal dog's owner, half joking, to the dog
readings.reading: playful, delighted; fast; a laugh at the end

readings.character: A roommate pointing at a pile of dirty dishes
readings.reading: dry sarcasm; drawn-out "finally"; stress on "exactly"; a sigh

readings.character: A soldier's comrade, relieved they survived
readings.reading: relief; breath out first; quiet, rough voice

readings.character: A ghost in an empty house
readings.reading: distant and hollow; very slow; whispered second sentence
